title: Sanitation programme and zoned inspection checks
moduleTitle: Group (Cleaning & Hygiene): Quality, evidence and handover
audience: Supervisors and leads who write, run or inspect a sanitation programme in a food plant, store or service zone.
learningOutcomes: Write a sanitation programme that states each task, its frequency and the person responsible.
Inspect a food area by zone, marking each check yes or no and recording each deficiency.
Close a deficiency by correcting it, checking the correction and recording the result.
Explain why a written programme lets a new worker work out the tasks without help.

instruction.heading: Write the programme in specific terms
instruction.body: A sanitation programme is written so that a new worker can follow it without asking. Each task states what is done, where, how often and by whom. The source gives the example of one employee who scrapes and sprays a waste container weekly, another who cleans restrooms each day, and another who inspects monitoring devices and baiting points each day. Assigning named tasks to named people shows where responsibility sits and lets management see whether the programme is being done. A checklist is a useful way to assign the duties.

instruction.heading: Inspect by zone with a yes or no record
instruction.body: A preventive programme depends on regular inspection. The inspection form is matched to the business, but in general it covers zones such as the exterior grounds, the building exterior, the building interior, dry and refrigerated storage, preparation areas, dishwashing, the indoor waste area, toilets and locker rooms, the lunch room, utility and office areas, and public areas. Each item is marked yes or no. A no marks a deficiency that must be corrected, and the entry on the far side of the form notes what is wrong. The inspection record is then reviewed and signed by the responsible person. This lesson does not reproduce any published inspection form; the zone structure is described in new words.

instruction.heading: Close deficiencies and keep the record honest
instruction.body: A deficiency found on inspection is recorded, corrected and checked. Where pest evidence or poor housekeeping is found, the inspector logs it, assigns the corrective action to a named person and sets a date for re-inspection. A zone that looks clean is not passed until each item on the form has been checked. Records are completed during the inspection itself and are not filled in later from memory. A checklist with every item ticked and no deficiencies recorded, when problems were seen, is a false record.

procedure: Confirm the zone list and the checklist for the area, and the inspection date and time.
Work through each zone, marking each item yes or no.
Record each no as a deficiency, with the location and what was seen.
Assign each corrective action to a named person with a due date.
Recheck each corrected item and mark it as closed with the date.
Review and sign the inspection record, and report any pest evidence to the responsible person (see “Pest control principles for food plants, stores and food-service zones”).

workedExamples.situation: A supervisor inspects a dry store and sees pest evidence near a pallet stack and a box of empty, unsealed containers stored against the wall.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is recorded, and what are the next steps?
workedExamples.reasoning: The supervisor marks the pest-evidence item and the storage item as no, records the locations, assigns the pest report to the responsible person, assigns the storage correction to a named worker, and sets a re-inspection date.

equipmentAndPpe: Current inspection checklist for the area
Gloves and eye protection where contact is needed

commonErrors.error: Ticking every item without looking at each zone.
commonErrors.prevention: Check each item in the zone and mark it on the day, with evidence.

commonErrors.error: Recording a deficiency but not assigning a correction.
commonErrors.prevention: Every no has a named action and a due date.

commonErrors.error: Completing the record after the shift from memory.
commonErrors.prevention: Complete the record while the inspection is under way.

commonErrors.error: Passing a zone before the re-inspection is done.
commonErrors.prevention: A deficiency is closed only after it has been rechecked.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Inspection of food areas may involve chemicals, wet floors and pests. Follow the safety rules in “Processing-plant wet cleaning: dry removal, drains and protein-safe rinsing”, “Pest control principles for food plants, stores and food-service zones” and “Dry waste areas and waste containers as pest and contamination sources” during the inspection.
Where an inspection finds a hazard the worker cannot control, the inspection stops in that zone and the responsible person is informed.
The inspection structure described here is general practice.

qualityStandard: Each zone on the list is inspected and every item is marked yes or no.
Each deficiency has a location, a corrective action, a named person and a due date.
Each corrected item is rechecked before it is closed.
The record is completed while the inspection runs and is then signed.
documentationEvidence: Completed checklist with yes and no marks for each zone.
Deficiency log with corrective action, owner and due date.
summary: A written programme names each task, frequency and person.
Inspect each zone and mark each item yes or no, on the day.
Every deficiency has an action, an owner and a re-check.
A false record is worse than a failed zone.

knowledgeChecks.question: What makes an inspection checklist useful?
options: It lists only the good results and leaves out every item that failed or was not checked
It is filled in once a year by the owner at the same time each year and signed
Each item is marked yes or no, and deficiencies are recorded with a corrective action
It replaces the cleaning schedule and the training log for the whole team

knowledgeChecks.question: Why assign specific sanitation tasks to specific people?
options: Because the law requires one name per task for every single task on the site
To avoid any need for training and to save the cost of the staff
So staff do not need written instructions and no one needs to check the work
So responsibility and frequency are clear and performance can be checked

knowledgeChecks.question: A deficiency is found on inspection. What is the correct next step?
options: Record it, correct it and check that the correction is completed
Leave it if the area looks clean and tidy and no one has complained
Tell the supervisor after the next shift and then keep working as normal
Remove the item from the checklist and file the page away
